objective: Expand the unbounded-girth LPS spectral input into an all-cut proof, a deterministic exact selector and a 12-regular fixed-d root-negation candidate; audit the degree-four limitation.

atomic_claims.text: In an r-regular graph, every shore of size s satisfies |delta(A)| >= (r-lambda_2)s(n-s)/n; a Laplacian gap greater than two excludes MC.
Deleting a spanning subgraph of maximum degree t decreases edge expansion by at most t.

From the attributed LPS/prime input, deleting two successive perfect matchings yields a deterministic family of simple connected bipartite 12-regular graphs, girth at least g, and all cuts larger than the smaller shore.
Fix d0=13; for every integer g>=3 the family has average degree 12<13, girth>=g, and no matching cut, without using small-order conventions.
A finite simple 4-regular graph of girth at least eight has lambda_2>=2, so the strict gap test alone cannot certify no-MC in that class.

assumptions: Frozen finite simple graph and two nonempty shore semantics are unchanged.
The LPS existence/spectrum/girth theorem, Dirichlet and quadratic reciprocity are explicitly attributed pending theorem dependencies, not newly admitted axioms.
Finite spectral linear algebra, the integer PSD test and the perfect-matching proof require their own review.
All family choices are deterministic finite searches with termination proved from the stated inputs, not claimed efficient implementations.
risks: No graph generator, SAT solver, spectral computation, proof assistant or mathematical verifier was executed.
The exact LPS specialization was read in the 2025 primary paper; the original 1988 full proof was not accessible here.
The root and its source-faithfulness dependency remain open in the trusted ledger; publication, CI and merge are not EvidenceLinks.
The degree-four sufficient-test limitation is not an assertion that all such graphs have MC.
Earlier C12/C13 transport assertions were contradicted by fresh GETs and corrected in Issue #3; this packet uses only actual main.
